# dsh-searxng-search
Keyless `web_search` for DeepSeek Harness via a self-hosted SearXNG instance. A thin `ctx.web` provi
der (`searxng-local`) plus on-demand `podman start` — no API key, no MCP hop. The start is detached
into a transient systemd scope, so restarting `dsh-web` cannot kill the container's port-forward (se
transient systemd scope, so restarting `dsh-web` cannot kill the container's port-forward (see why).
## Install
One-liner for `podman` (system dependency, outside pnpm):

Install the bundle into your `web` profile (pnpm only — no profile hand-editing):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Verify the layer without booting:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart `dsh web` for the new bundle layer to take effect. Build artifacts (`lib/`) are committ
ed, so installing from git runs no build and needs no pnpm `allowBuilds` approval. The first search
creates the container if missing (~1–2 min for the image pull), later ones start it on demand after
the container if missing (~1–2 min for the image pull), later ones start it on demand after reboots.
### Why the container start is scoped
`podman run` / `podman start` inherit the cgroup of whoever invokes them. Installed as a bundle that
caller is `dsh-web.service`, so the container's `conmon` and `pasta` — the processes that actually
own the `127.0.0.1:8888` forward — end up inside that service's cgroup. A `systemctl --user restart
dsh-web` then tears the cgroup down with the default `KillMode=control-group`: SearXNG keeps running
, but nothing listens on the port any more, so `web_search` reports the provider down while `podman
ps` still shows the container `Up`.
Every container-mutating CLI call is therefore wrapped in a transient per-container scope:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A scope is a *sibling* of `dsh-web.service` under `user@1000.service/app.slice`, so restarting DSH n
ever touches it. Inspect it with `systemctl --user status dsh-searxng-searxng.scope`. Where no user
systemd manager is reachable (macOS, a bare CI container, `systemd-run` missing) the plugin calls th
e CLI directly and logs a one-line warning; `SEARXNG_DETACH=0` forces that behaviour. `searxng-podma
n.sh` uses the same wrapper.
The bundle pins `searchProvider: searxng-local` in its own layer because the base bundle defaults to
`deepseek-official` (hosted API, needs a key) — without the pin, searches never reach your local in
stance. Your profile patch can still override it. To go back to hosted search, `dsh plugin --profile
web remove dsh-searxng-search` (then restart) and the layer — pin included — is gone.
Local development: `pnpm install && pnpm build`, then `dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/ds
`pnpm install && pnpm build`, then `dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-searxng-search`.
